correctness.rationale: The original mathematics is correct, including the removed exchange claim. A fresh implementation (not either uploaded verifier) checked all 65,536 placements and independently ran BFS from all 320 minimum triples. It reproduced failed counts 1,16,120,240,60 and none above size four, exact equality of failures with subsets of induced 2K2s, unique extension for every failed triple, and at most one wave after initial observation for every success. It also reproduced degree 21, 3360 edges and shells (1,21,126,172) at all 320 roots for the original graph. Replay: /workspace/branches/42a07edb-32ce-4794-99f4-9daa907203a4/reproduce_record2.py and its reproduction_subsets.json and reproduction_exchange.json. For the repaired claim I independently checked the written proof: wave monotonicity follows because a forcer remains observed and an unobserved target remains unique in the larger observed state. The three triple orbits use a translated vertex of the appropriate type; the XOR representatives have the listed initial unseen sets and wave behavior. For an edge represented by ∅,{i}, the six nonneighbors of both endpoints induce three pairs of complementary two-subsets of the other four coordinates. This supplies the unique completion and the count 40·3/2. For the failed representative {0,1,6}, adding its partner 7 leaves the observed set unchanged, so the completed set is stalled. Every pair extends to a failed triple; a four-set with one edge in every triple is a matching by counting twice per edge, and such a five-set would require 3e=10. The complete failure classification and polynomial follow, without an exchange enumeration. Repaired RESULT.md, SLOGAN.txt and scientific body of VERIFICATION.md were checked for consistency; the verification-status front matter is unchanged.

The same-day Shrikhande classification is an all-subset theorem on a different sixteen-vertex Cayley graph. Its maximal failures are 32 triangles and 12 cyclic lines, and it has successful pairs.

Remaining work beyond that classification is to prove exhaustion of failures of size ≥4 and determine the exact extensions: the common-nonneighbor subgraph of each edge is three disjoint edges, and adjoining the compelled partner leaves the failed representative's closed-neighborhood union unchanged.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A minimum-triple classification certifies success for supersets of those triples. It does not certify failure of supersets of failed triples, because adding vertices can create successful placements even without a successful triple. The matching/unchanged-observation proof plus the all-size edge count are the required additions. The repaired global one-wave bound is then a corollary, not a stand-alone originality claim.

value.rationale: The repaired finding is an exact structural classification on a canonical strongly regular graph, not a recomputation of minimum size or jump distances. It identifies all maximal ways to fail, gives a unique completion rule for each failing triple and specifies the success enumerator at every sensor budget. Those are distinct useful finite facts for reasoning about robustness of placements. The proof explains why the induced matchings stall, beyond simply listing the configurations.
